newsitem.title: UK: World must learn Bosnian lesson-Irish president.
newsitem.headline: World must learn Bosnian lesson-Irish president.

text.p: Irish President Mary Robinson said on Tuesday the world had to learn the lessons of Bosnia and Rwanda and develop new institutions capable of long-term political action to resolve the causes of such conflicts.
"Complex political crises cannot be resolved by short-term humanitarian responses alone," she said in a lecture prepared for delivery to the English Speaking Union in London.
Robinson is considered a possible candidate to succeed Boutros Boutros-Ghali as U.N. Secretary-General.

Aid workers and human rights monitors had learnt from experience that "international humanitarian aid in itself, and alone, is not the solution to the problems of the people of Rwanda or other crisis areas, and may simply postpone the problem so that it recurs", Robinson said.
She looked at the present international institutions and found them wanting.

For example, she wondered why the role of confronting "intimidators" in camps for Rwandan refugees in Zaire -- the extremists who had committed genocide in Rwanda -- was left to aid workers and not taken up by the international community.

The camps set up in eastern Zaire and Tanzania were a response to the Rwandan crisis in 1994 but not a solution, she said. "The camps represented a paralysis of any dynamic towards a true settlement."
That paralysis has been broken over the past month by rebel Zaireans, whose attacks on the camps caused the extremists to flee and prompted up to 600,000 refugees to return to Rwanda.
Robinson saw the beginnings of a new approach in the response to the military coup in Burundi in July.
Leaders of surrounding east African states quickly imposed sanctions on Burundi, and sent in respected politicians, like Julius Nyerere, a former president of Tanzania, to mediate.
The European Union backed up this effort by dispatching a special envoy, Aldo Ajello, in a supportive role.

Robinson praised this African-driven, European-backed initiative, and called, as a next step, for a conference on peace, security and development to be held under the aegis of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.
Robinson did not mention the conflict in the British province of Northern Ireland. As constitutional head of the Irish state, she cannot comment on Irish politics.
